overview.headline: Continuous circulation of water through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation and runoff

keyPoints.point: The hydrologic cycle involves continuous circulation of water between ground and atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

keyPoints.point: Evaporation is the change of liquid water to gas and needs energy to occur.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyPoints.point: Transpiration is evaporation of water from plants through stomata, with most water passing to the atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Condensation changes water vapor to liquid, appears as clouds or dew, and releases heat that can aid hurricane formation.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Precipitation delivers fresh water as rain, snow, hail or sleet when condensed particles grow too heavy to stay aloft.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation is the primary way we receive fresh water on Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: change of state from liquid to gas that requires energy
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: evaporation of water from plants through stomata on leaves
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: process where water vapor becomes liquid forming clouds or dew
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: primary way fresh water falls to Earth as rain, snow, hail or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation is the primary way we receive fresh water on Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: excess precipitation flowing over saturated ground into rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).
